title: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
notes: v1 submitted 2026-10-15. Defines twelve approval-path attacks (AB1 to AB12); Table 4 runs five against AP2 at commit e1ea56d (v0.2.0) and marks the other seven not applicable; section 3.3 says AP2's constraint layer rejected every executed binding attack, with a partial result for non-injective rendering in the sample card (AB6) and budget accumulation that depends on the integrator (AB12).

title: Protocol-Level Attacks on Agentic Commerce Platforms: A Cross-Platform Taxonomy, AIP-Bench, and Unified Defense
notes: v1 2026-07-23. Section 6, AP2 v0.2.0: 14 vulnerabilities, established by deterministic code proofs against the reference implementation, with A-AP2-11 also run live. The other platforms are CoralOS and Fetch.ai uAgents; the paper never names UCP or OpenAI's ACP (its one ACP is an agent communication protocol listed with A2A and CORAL in a companion paper). Its background text still describes AP2 with v0.1 Intent, Cart and Payment Mandates.
